exposure: Tranexamic acid (prophylactic use after umbilical-cord clamping)
outcome: Composite of maternal death or blood transfusion by hospital discharge or 7 days post partum
Estimated intraoperative blood loss of more than 1 liter
Interventions for bleeding and related complications
cohort: Participants undergoing cesarean delivery at 31 U.S. hospitals.
finding: Prophylactic use of tranexamic acid during cesarean delivery did not significantly lower the risk of a composite outcome of maternal death or blood transfusion compared to placebo.
followup_time: Up to 7 days post partum (or hospital discharge, whichever came first)
